questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA):
1. It was established in 1957 and is headquartered at Vienna.
2. It is a principal organ of the United Nations.
3. It grew out of the 'Atoms for Peace' proposal made by the US President at the UN in 1953.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The IAEA is an autonomous organisation within the UN system that reports to the General Assembly and the Security Council; it is not a principal organ or even a specialised agency. It was born from Eisenhower's 1953 proposal to pool nuclear materials for peaceful use.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the structure of the IAEA:
1. The General Conference of all member states meets annually.
2. The Board of Governors has 35 members.
3. The Director General is appointed by the UN Security Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Director General is appointed by the Board of Governors with the approval of the General Conference, not by the Security Council. The Board is the executive body that approves safeguards agreements.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about IAEA safeguards:
1. A comprehensive safeguards agreement is required of a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the NPT.
2. The Additional Protocol gives the IAEA greater access to detect undeclared nuclear activities.
3. India has a comprehensive safeguards agreement covering all its nuclear facilities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Comprehensive agreements apply to all nuclear material of NNWS in the NPT, and the Additional Protocol adds complementary access to catch undeclared material. India is outside the NPT and its safeguards cover only declared civilian facilities under an India-specific agreement, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Arrange the following steps in the India-US civil nuclear cooperation process in chronological order:
1. Manmohan Singh-George Bush Joint Statement
2. Hyde Act enacted by the US Congress
3. IAEA Board approves the India-specific safeguards agreement
4. NSG grants a waiver to India
5. India-US 123 Agreement signed
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The July 2005 joint statement led to the Hyde Act (December 2006). Then came the IAEA Board approval (1 August 2008), the NSG waiver (6 September 2008) and the signing of the 123 Agreement in October 2008.
questions.h: 2005 pledge, 2006 law, Aug IAEA, Sep NSG, Oct signature.

questions.q: The Nobel Peace Prize of 2005 was awarded jointly to the IAEA and which of the following persons?
questions.e: The IAEA and its Director General Mohamed ElBaradei received the 2005 prize for efforts to prevent nuclear energy being used for military purposes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG):
1. It was formed in response to India's nuclear test of 1974.
2. Its guidelines for nuclear transfers are published by the IAEA as INFCIRC/254.
3. It takes decisions by majority vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The NSG (first met 1975, hence the 'London Club') was created to control exports of nuclear items after the 1974 test showed that civilian technology could be diverted. It works by consensus, so a single participant can block an applicant.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India is not a full participant in the Nuclear Suppliers Group.
Statement-II: The waiver granted by the NSG to India in 2008 made it a participating government of the NSG.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 2008 waiver only allowed NSG members to trade in nuclear items with India despite its non-NPT status. India applied for full membership in 2016, which has not been granted.
questions.s: MEA; NSG Statement on Civil Nuclear Cooperation with India, 6 Sep 2008

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Zangger Committee:
1. It was set up in 1971 to interpret the export-control provisions of Article III(2) of the NPT.
2. It maintains a 'Trigger List' of items that trigger IAEA safeguards on export.
3. India is a member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Committee, also called the NPT Exporters Committee, builds a Trigger List for items whose export requires safeguards. India is not in the NPT and is not a member.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the CTBT Organization (CTBTO):
1. Its Preparatory Commission is headquartered in Vienna.
2. It will become a full organisation only after the treaty enters into force.
3. Its International Monitoring System uses seismic, hydroacoustic, infrasound and radionuclide technologies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CTBTO exists as a Preparatory Commission because the treaty is not in force. The IMS detects explosions through four techniques, and the Vienna-based commission also runs the International Data Centre.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Wassenaar Arrangement:
1. It controls the transfer of conventional arms and dual-use goods and technologies.
2. It was set up in 1996 as the successor to the Cold War-era COCOM.
3. India became a participating state in 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Wassenaar is an informal export-control regime with a Secretariat in Vienna. It replaced COCOM, which had restricted exports to the Soviet bloc, and India was admitted in December 2017.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Export control regime) with List-II (Focus):
List-I
A. Nuclear Suppliers Group
B. Missile Technology Control Regime
C. Wassenaar Arrangement
D. Australia Group
List-II
1. Chemical and biological weapons precursors and equipment
2. Nuclear materials and technology
3. Rocket and unmanned aerial delivery systems
4. Conventional arms and dual-use items
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: NSG covers nuclear items, MTCR covers missiles and UAVs, Wassenaar covers conventional arms and dual-use items, and the Australia Group controls chemical and biological items.
questions.s: Websites of the four regimes; MEA

questions.q:
Consider the following export control regimes:
1. Missile Technology Control Regime
2. Wassenaar Arrangement
3. Australia Group
4. Nuclear Suppliers Group
How many of the above is India currently a member of?
questions.e: India joined the MTCR in 2016, Wassenaar in 2017 and the Australia Group in 2018. Its application to the NSG remains pending, so it is not a member.
questions.s: MEA, India and Multilateral Export Control Regimes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Australia Group:
1. It was formed in 1985 after chemical weapons were used in the Iran-Iraq war.
2. It is a legally binding treaty with a verification body.
3. It harmonises export controls on chemical and biological items.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Australia Group is an informal arrangement with no treaty or inspectorate; the Chemical Weapons Convention and OPCW are separate. It exists so that exports from member states do not help make chemical or biological weapons.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR):
1. It was formed in 1987 by the G-7 countries.
2. It is a legally binding treaty.
3. India joined it in 2016.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The MTCR is a voluntary, informal political understanding to limit proliferation of missiles and UAVs capable of carrying a 500 kg payload at least 300 km. Membership let India buy advanced missile and drone technology and sell certain items.

questions.q:
Arrange the following export control regimes in the chronological order of their establishment:
1. Missile Technology Control Regime
2. Wassenaar Arrangement
3. Nuclear Suppliers Group
4. Australia Group
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The NSG came first (1974-75), then the Australia Group (1985), the MTCR (1987) and Wassenaar (1996).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ITER:
1. The project's site is Cadarache in France.
2. India is one of its members.
3. It is designed to demonstrate nuclear fission.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ITER is an international experiment to show that fusion can generate energy on a large scale. Its members are China, the EU, India, Japan, South Korea, Russia and the United States.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Nuclear Security Summit venues in the order in which the summits were held:
1. Seoul
2. Washington
3. The Hague
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The series, begun by President Obama, ran Washington (2010), Seoul (2012), The Hague (2014) and Washington (2016).

questions.q:
Statement-I: The IAEA is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
Statement-II: The IAEA reports annually to the General Assembly and, when needed, to the Security Council.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The IAEA is an independent organisation related to the UN through a special agreement, not a specialised agency under Articles 57 and 63. Its reporting lines to both the Assembly and the Council are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Conference on Disarmament:
1. It is the sole multilateral disarmament negotiating forum of the international community and is based in Geneva.
2. It works by consensus.
3. India is not a member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Conference negotiated the NPT, the CWC and the CTBT, and India has been a member since the early 1960s. Its consensus rule has stalled new negotiations for years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW):
1. Its headquarters is at The Hague.
2. It implements the Chemical Weapons Convention.
3. It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2013.
4. India completed the destruction of its declared chemical weapons stockpile by 2009.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All four are correct. OPCW inspectors verify destruction, and India's declared stockpile was verified destroyed in 2009, which is why India is counted among the states that met the CWC obligation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA):
1. It was concluded at Vienna in July 2015 between Iran and China, France, Germany, Russia, the UK and the US.
2. The Security Council endorsed it through Resolution 2231.
3. India was a signatory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The IAEA monitors Iran's commitments under the deal. India was not a party to the negotiations or the agreement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about AUKUS:
1. It is a security partnership of Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States announced in September 2021.
2. Its first pillar provides for nuclear-powered submarines for Australia.
3. India is a member.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: AUKUS is a trilateral pact; India belongs to the Quad, which is separate. The submarine plan raised questions on safeguards under the NPT because naval reactors use nuclear material.
questions.s: White House / UK Government joint statement, 15 Sep 2021

questions.q: Which one of the following organisations is NOT headquartered in Vienna?
o: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons
questions.e: The OPCW is at The Hague. The IAEA, the CTBTO and UNIDO are all based in Vienna.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the order in which India became a member:
1. Australia Group
2. Missile Technology Control Regime
3. Wassenaar Arrangement
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: India joined the MTCR in June 2016, Wassenaar in December 2017 and the Australia Group in January 2018.
questions.s: MEA, India and Multilateral Export Control Regimes

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Nuclear and Radiological Event Scale (INES):
1. It was developed jointly by the IAEA and the OECD Nuclear Energy Agency.
2. Chernobyl and Fukushima Daiichi were both rated at Level 7.
3. Three Mile Island was rated at Level 7.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Level 7 is a 'major accident'. Three Mile Island (1979) was a Level 5 accident with wider consequences, not a Level 7.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT):
1. It was opened for signature in 1968 and entered into force in 1970.
2. It recognises as nuclear-weapon states those that manufactured and exploded a device before 1 January 1967.
3. It was extended for a fixed period of 25 years in 1995.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1995 Review and Extension Conference extended the NPT indefinitely, not for 25 years. The 1967 cut-off gives five nuclear-weapon states: the US, Russia, the UK, France and China.

questions.q: Under which Article of the NPT can a party withdraw by giving three months' notice to all other parties and the Security Council?
questions.e: Article X allows withdrawal if extraordinary events jeopardise a party's supreme interests, with three months' notice. North Korea announced its withdrawal in 2003. Article VI is the disarmament undertaking.

questions.q:
Statement-I: India has refused to sign the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.
Statement-II: India regards the NPT as discriminatory because it divides states into nuclear-weapon 'haves' and non-nuclear 'have-nots' with no time-bound disarmament.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: India has consistently argued that the treaty freezes a nuclear hierarchy based on a 1967 cut-off date, which is the reason it has stayed out. India, Pakistan and Israel have never joined.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT):
1. It was opened for signature in 1996.
2. India has signed but not ratified it.
3. Its entry into force requires ratification by 44 specified states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India never signed the CTBT. When India refused consensus in the Conference on Disarmament in 1996, the text was taken to the General Assembly, which adopted it. The 44 states listed in Annex 2 are those that had nuclear reactors in 1996.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The CTBT has not yet entered into force although it was adopted in 1996.
Statement-II: Its entry into force depends on ratification by all 44 states listed in Annex 2 of the treaty.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Several Annex 2 states have either not signed (India, Pakistan, North Korea) or not ratified (for example the US, China, Israel, Egypt and Iran) the treaty. Until all 44 ratify, the treaty cannot enter into force.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW):
1. It was adopted at the UN in July 2017.
2. It entered into force in January 2021.
3. India has signed it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The TPNW entered into force on 22 January 2021 after the 50th ratification. India did not take part in the negotiations and has not signed it. The campaign group ICAN won the 2017 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons entered into force in 2021.
Statement-II: None of the nuclear-armed states has joined it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are true. The nuclear-armed states stayed away, saying the treaty ignores the security conditions that deter war, but that fact is not the reason it came into force in 2021, which followed the 50th ratification.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Partial Test Ban Treaty of 1963:
1. It banned nuclear tests in the atmosphere, in outer space and under water.
2. India was among the countries that signed it in 1963.
3. It banned underground nuclear tests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Underground tests were left outside the ban because of verification difficulties, which is why they continued until the CTBT. India signed in August 1963.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Outer Space Treaty of 1967:
1. It prohibits placing nuclear weapons or other weapons of mass destruction in orbit around the Earth.
2. It prohibits national appropriation of the Moon and other celestial bodies.
3. It permits placing nuclear weapons on the Moon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The treaty reserves the Moon and other celestial bodies exclusively for peaceful purposes, so weapons of any kind may not be installed there.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Nuclear-weapon-free zone treaty) with List-II (Region):
List-I
A. Treaty of Pelindaba
B. Treaty of Rarotonga
C. Treaty of Tlatelolco
D. Treaty of Bangkok
List-II
1. Latin America and the Caribbean
2. Africa
3. South Pacific
4. South-East Asia
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Tlatelolco (1967) covers Latin America and the Caribbean, Rarotonga (1985) the South Pacific, Bangkok (1995) South-East Asia and Pelindaba (1996) Africa.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Antarctic Treaty:
1. It was signed in 1959.
2. India acceded to it in 1983.
3. It permits the establishment of military bases for defence.
4. It allows territorial claims to be extended.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Treaty, signed at Washington in 1959, reserves Antarctica for peaceful purposes and bars military bases and weapons tests. Article IV freezes existing claims and bars new ones. India acceded in 1983.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Geneva Conventions:
1. There are four Geneva Conventions, adopted in 1949.
2. Three Additional Protocols were adopted, in 1977 and 2005.
3. The International Committee of the Red Cross is a body of the United Nations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ICRC is a private, neutral Swiss humanitarian body, not a UN organ, although the Conventions give it a recognised role. Protocols I and II came in 1977 and Protocol III in 2005.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Biological Weapons Convention has an inspection body like the OPCW for verification.
Statement-II: The Convention prohibits the development, production and stockpiling of biological and toxin weapons.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The BWC (opened 1972, in force 1975) has no verification organisation, only a small Implementation Support Unit. The ban in Statement-II is accurate.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chemical Weapons Convention:
1. It entered into force in 1997.
2. India ratified it in 1996.
3. It allows states to retain their stockpiles indefinitely.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CWC requires destruction of all declared stockpiles under OPCW verification. India was an original signatory and ratified it in 1996.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer (1985) preceded the Montreal Protocol (1987).
2. The Kigali Amendment (2016) seeks to phase down chlorofluorocarbons.
3. India ratified the Kigali Amendment in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Kigali targets hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which replaced CFCs but are potent greenhouse gases. CFCs were phased out under the original Montreal Protocol.

questions.q:
Match List-I (Convention) with List-II (Subject):
List-I
A. Basel Convention
B. Rotterdam Convention
C. Stockholm Convention
D. Minamata Convention
List-II
1. Persistent organic pollutants
2. Mercury
3. Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes
4. Prior informed consent for trade in hazardous chemicals and pesticides
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Basel (1989) governs hazardous waste movements, Rotterdam (1998) the PIC procedure, Stockholm (2001) POPs and Minamata (2013) mercury.
questions.s: Secretariats of the BRS and Minamata Conventions (brsmeas.org; mercuryconvention.org)

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of adoption:
1. CITES
2. Ramsar Convention
3. Convention on Migratory Species
4. World Heritage Convention
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Ramsar (1971), the World Heritage Convention (1972), CITES (1973) and the Bonn Convention on Migratory Species (1979).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD):
1. It was opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit in 1992.
2. The Cartagena Protocol deals with biosafety.
3. The Nagoya Protocol deals with biosafety.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Nagoya Protocol (2010) deals with access to genetic resources and fair sharing of benefits (ABS); biosafety is the Cartagena Protocol (2000).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), 1982:
1. It came into force in 1994.
2. The Exclusive Economic Zone extends up to 12 nautical miles from the baseline.
3. India ratified it in 1995.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The territorial sea extends up to 12 nautical miles and the EEZ up to 200 nautical miles from the baseline.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the High Seas Treaty (BBNJ Agreement):
1. It was adopted in 2023 under UNCLOS.
2. It entered into force in January 2026.
3. It regulates biodiversity within the exclusive economic zones of coastal states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Agreement covers marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction, meaning the high seas and the seabed beyond EEZs. It entered into force on 17 January 2026 after reaching 60 ratifications.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Criminal Court (ICC):
1. The Rome Statute was adopted in 1998 and entered into force in 2002.
2. The Court sits at The Hague.
3. India is a party to the Rome Statute.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ICC is separate from the UN's International Court of Justice and tries individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression. India has not joined the Rome Statute.

questions.q:
Consider the following international instruments:
1. Ottawa Convention on anti-personnel mines
2. Convention on Cluster Munitions
3. Arms Trade Treaty
4. Chemical Weapons Convention
How many of the above is India NOT a party to?
questions.e: India has not joined the Ottawa Convention, the Convention on Cluster Munitions or the Arms Trade Treaty, but it is a party to the Chemical Weapons Convention.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961:
1. It was adopted in 1961.
2. A diplomatic agent enjoys immunity from the criminal jurisdiction of the receiving state.
3. The receiving state must give reasons before declaring a diplomat persona non grata.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Under Article 9 the receiving state may declare a diplomat persona non grata at any time without having to explain its decision. Article 29 declares diplomats inviolable and Article 31 gives immunity from criminal jurisdiction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the aftermath of the Chernobyl accident:
1. The accident occurred in 1986.
2. Within months, the IAEA adopted the Convention on Early Notification of a Nuclear Accident and the Convention on Assistance in Case of a Nuclear Accident.
3. The Convention on Nuclear Safety was adopted before the accident.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Chernobyl showed that nuclear fallout ignores borders, so states agreed in 1986 on prompt notification and mutual assistance. The Convention on Nuclear Safety came later, in 1994.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD):
1. It was adopted in 1994.
2. India hosted its 14th Conference of the Parties in 2019.
3. Its Secretariat is located at Nairobi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The UNCCD Secretariat is in Bonn, while Nairobi hosts UNEP. COP14 was held at Greater Noida in September 2019.
